identifiedRisks.description: Extreme technical complexity involving unproven technologies like the large-scale rotating centrifuge set, front projection systems, and zero-gravity rigs.
identifiedRisks.mitigation: Allocate significant budget for R&D, pre-visualization, and testing. Hire top-tier engineering and SFX teams.

identifiedRisks.description: Groundbreaking and extensive VFX requirements (205+ shots), including the abstract Stargate sequence, with high potential for schedule and budget overruns.
identifiedRisks.mitigation: Engage VFX supervisor from early prep. Budget for extensive motion control photography and optical printing. Build in contingency for VFX.

identifiedRisks.description: Requirement for numerous, large, and highly detailed sets (Discovery Centrifuge, Space Station, Moon Base) which are costly and time-consuming to build.
identifiedRisks.mitigation: Secure large-scale studio space well in advance. Detailed construction plans and budget must be locked early.

identifiedRisks.description: High-risk production elements including work with a trained lion, numerous other animals, and child actors, all of which have significant safety, logistical, and regulatory implications.
identifiedRisks.mitigation: Hire experienced animal wranglers and safety coordinators. Adhere strictly to child labor laws. Increase insurance coverage.

identifiedRisks.description: A long and complex production schedule (145 shooting days) with many dependencies between departments (e.g., SFX, VFX, stunts) increases the likelihood of cascading delays.
identifiedRisks.mitigation: Utilize advanced scheduling software. Build in contingency days for complex sequences. Ensure clear communication between department heads.

processingEvidence.details: Simulated lookup of union rates. Assumed a UK/US co-production. Using BECTU/PACT 2024 Major Feature Agreement rates for UK-based crew and SAG-AFTRA Theatrical Agreement rates for US-based principal cast. Rates validated for all key positions based on project scale and complexity.
assumptions: Jurisdiction: UK for Below-the-Line Crew (BECTU), US for Above-the-Line Cast (SAG-AFTRA).
Rates are representative of a high-budget, major studio production.
All rates are current and include no projected increases during production.

processingEvidence.details: Calculated base wages for all identified cast and crew. Applied weekly rates for long-term engagements and daily rates for short-term players. Prep (12 weeks) and wrap (2 weeks) periods factored into crew contracts. Cast contracts based on scheduled shoot days plus hold days.
assumptions: Production Schedule: 145 shoot days over 29 weeks.
Core Crew Contract: 12 weeks prep + 29 weeks shoot + 2 weeks wrap = 43 weeks total.
Cast weekly rates are based on a 5-day week.

processingEvidence.details: Estimated overtime based on schedule analysis. Scenes with long shoot times (10+ hours), DAY_TO_NIGHT transitions, and complex technical setups (Centrifuge, Stargate) were identified as high-OT risks. A blended overtime factor of 28% has been applied to BTL crew base wages. A lump sum for meal and turnaround penalties has been included.
assumptions: Standard work day is 10 hours for crew.
Overtime calculated at 1.5x for hours 11-12, and 2.0x beyond 12 hours.
The 28% factor is an aggregate estimate across the entire production schedule.

processingEvidence.details: Calculated all statutory and union-mandated fringe benefits. Applied UK rates to all crew gross wages and US rates to all cast gross wages.

ukCrewFringes.description: Applied to total gross wages (base + OT + allowances)

processingEvidence.details: Applied location-based costs for the 'Phase 1: The Dawn of Man' shoot in Africa. Calculated travel, per diems, and a hazard/uplift premium for the 20-day shoot block.

positions.title: Director
positions.notes: Fee not included in labor; typically a separate ATL deal with profit participation.

travelAndPerDiem.description: Travel, lodging, and per diems for Africa shoot.

laborCostRisks.description: Overtime Escalation: The high number of complex scenes with long setup and shoot times (e.g., Centrifuge, Stargate, Ape sequences) creates a significant risk of overtime costs exceeding the 28% estimate.
laborCostRisks.mitigation: Strict enforcement of daily schedules by AD team. Pre-lighting and rigging on separate days where possible. The 15% contingency is designed to cover this risk.

laborCostRisks.description: Union Rate Increases: The production spans multiple years, making it vulnerable to scheduled union rate increases not factored into the initial budget.
laborCostRisks.mitigation: Budget for a 3-5% annual escalation in labor rates. Lock in key personnel with multi-year contracts where possible.

laborCostRisks.description: Specialty Labor Shortage: The demand for highly specialized crew (motion control, prosthetics, large-scale riggers) could lead to higher-than-budgeted rates due to limited availability.
laborCostRisks.mitigation: Identify and contract key specialty personnel early in pre-production.

laborCostRisks.description: Cast/Crew Burnout: The long and demanding schedule increases the risk of illness or injury, leading to costly production delays and potential replacement costs.
laborCostRisks.mitigation: Enforce mandatory rest periods and turnaround times. Ensure adequate on-set medical and safety support. Maintain a robust insurance policy.

riskAssessment.contingencyRecommendation: A 15% contingency on total labor costs is recommended due to the unprecedented technical complexity, long schedule, and high-risk sequences involving stunts and special effects. This provides a buffer of approximately $2.1M to cover potential overages in overtime, penalties, and other unforeseen labor expenses.
